title: kv-cache-attn-kernel-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-10
content:
Goal: track/debug flaky misaligned KV-cache reads that only show up for long sequences (>= 4096) when the attention kernel selection picks the fused path.

Symptoms observed:
- For a small subset of prompts with seqlen > 4096, generated output suddenly repeats token prefixes or returns garbled text mid-stream.
- Happens intermittently in production traffic but easily reproduced locally when forcing certain kernel combinations or increasing batch size to 2+.
- Error in logs (rare) shows a kv cache size mismatch: "kv_cache_size 32768 != expected_kv_size 65536" — looks like half-size reads.
- Reproducer attached: run_infer_longseqlen.sh (below).

Commands / runs tried (local, docker image: redwood/serving:debug-2025-11):
1) baseline reproducer (single request):
   ./run_infer_longseqlen.sh --model rwd-gpt-13b --seqlen 4608 --batch 1
   -> baseline: works (rare failure)

2) force fused attention kernel (env var):
   RWD_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL=fused ./run_infer_longseqlen.sh --seqlen 4608 --batch 2
   -> failure reproduces in ~7/10 runs (consistent)

3) force matmul (fallback) kernel:
   RWD_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL=matmul ./run_infer_longseqlen.sh --seqlen 4608 --batch 2
   -> no failure observed (10/10 runs)

4) run with DEBUG=1 and KV_CHECK=1 (extra asserts in runtime):
   DEBUG=1 KV_CHECK=1 ./run_infer_longseqlen.sh --seqlen 4608 --batch 2 2>&1 | tee debug-kv.log
   -> saw assertion: "kv_index_wrap: computed_idx < stored_idx (wrap detected)" before output corruption

5) turned on ASAN for the fused attention path, re-ran repro under gdb:
   ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_stack_use_after_return=1 gdb --args ./serving_binary --request-file repro.json
   -> no heap corruption detected; backtrace points to fused_attention::write_kv (kv_indexing.cpp:174)

6) ran small C++ unit: tests/kv_indexing_test.cpp (designed to simulate circular buffer wrap with seqlen offsets), increased iterations -> occasionally fails when offset counter overflows 16-bit boundary.

Logs / error snippets (excerpt):
--- debug-kv.log ---
[2025-11-05T14:22:13.512Z] INFO kernel_selector: picked kernel fused_attention (sm80, sm86)
[2025-11-05T14:22:13.513Z] DEBUG kv_cache: write_pos=32768 write_len=1024 new_write_pos=33792
[2025-11-05T14:22:13.513Z] ERROR kv_cache: kv_cache_size 32768 != expected_kv_size 65536
[2025-11-05T14:22:13.514Z] WARN runtime: packet dropped, falling back to fallback model variant
--- end ---

Hypotheses so far:
- Hypothesis A: index overflow due to 16-bit index type used in fused kernel path. When sequence length * batch * num_heads exceeds 2^16 entries, the index wraps and writes into wrong positions.
  Evidence: unit test failing near 65536 boundary; errors show half-size values (32768).

- Hypothesis B: fused_attention uses a different KV buffer layout (interleaved per-head) and the kernel_selector incorrectly assumes same stride as matmul kernel, causing mis-sized memcpy for some architectures.
  Evidence: switching kernel to matmul avoids the issue; kernel_selector log shows 'assumed_stride=64' for fused but actual stride should be 128 in some cases.

- Hypothesis C: batching interaction — when batch >1, KV buffer base offsets per item are computed with an integer expr that truncates on certain compilers/opt flags (-O3 float->int conversions?), leading to misaligned base pointers.

Immediate repro notes / minimal steps:
1) Use docker redwood/serving:debug-2025-11 (image includes RWD_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL override).
2) Run: RWD_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL=fused ./run_infer_longseqlen.sh --model rwd-gpt-13b --seqlen 4608 --batch 2 --prompt-file long_prompt.txt
3) If failure happens, inspect /tmp/kv-dump-<pid>.bin (we added KV_DUMP=1 env to dump buffer) and compare expected offsets using kv_inspect.py (in tools/).

Observations from kv_inspect.py on a failing run:
- header: total_entries=65536 stride=64 head_dim=64
- found non-monotonic write indices: [0..32767] then restart at 0
- tail summaries show older token keys clobbered mid-request

Quick mitigation (hotfix):
- Force kernel selection to matmul path in runtime until root cause fixed: set RWD_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL=matmul via deployment rollout config. Verified no perf regression for these workloads in preliminary tests (throughput -5% p50).

Longer term fix ideas:
- Audit all index types in fused_attention and kv_indexing modules: ensure 32-bit (or 64-bit) counters where needed. Add unit tests around boundary values (65535 -> 65536 transitions).
- Add CI fuzz test that runs fused kernel with varying seqlen, batch sizes, and head counts to try to trigger overflow.
- Add runtime guard: if computed kv_size != expected, abort and log full context (dump KV pages) instead of silently falling back.
- Revisit kernel_selector heuristics to make sure stride/format assumptions are validated before picking fused kernel; add a validation pass during kernel selection that checks computed strides against buffer layout.

Open tasks / next steps:
- [ ] Create minimal C++ repro isolated from full runtime (WIP, tests/kv_repro_fused.cpp). Assigned to Katherine Liu. (JIRA-INF-784)
- [ ] Add integer width audit PR for fused_attention files. Assigned to me (Liam). Target: PR by 2025-11-14. (draft PR linked)
- [ ] Rollout runtime config to force matmul for prod tier-1 while patch lands. Owner: SRE (Ethan)
- [ ] Add CI job to run seqlen fuzzing on nightly GPU runners. Owner: infra-team.

Notes / random thoughts (scratch):
- Could be an AB test of different kernels getting toggled in prod (rollout percentage); check rollout logs for kernel_selector experiments (rolling config updates last week).
- If it is layout mismatch, might only appear on sm86 vs sm80 GPU archs; test matrix: A100, H100, L40.
- Need to correlate customer requests (which prompts) with tokenization patterns: rare prompts might trigger long expanded sequences due to many special tokens (metadata).

Reproducer script (local) - run_infer_longseqlen.sh (rough):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
IMG=redwood/serving:debug-2025-11
MODEL=${1:-rwd-gpt-13b}
SEQLEN=${2:-4608}
BATCH=${3:-2}
PROMPT=${4:-long_prompt.txt}

docker run --gpus all --rm -e RWD_MODEL=$MODEL -e RWD_SEQLEN=$SEQLEN -e RWD_BATCH=$BATCH -e KV_DUMP=1 -e RWD_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL=${RWD_FORCE_ATTENTION_KERNEL} -v $(pwd):/work -w /work $IMG ./serving_binary --request-file repro.json

(repro.json contains a single request with repeated tokens to reach needed seqlen)

Anything else to include here?
- I'll drop the raw kv-dump and failing binary to GCS (link in Jira) after next failing run.
- Katherine: results of your reduced repro would be helpful; if you can produce a single-threaded C++ demonstration that exercises fused kernel indexing that will speed up root cause.

TL;DR: failure correlates strongly with fused attention kernel on long sequences and batch>1; quick fix is to force matmul kernel. Likely root cause is integer width/stride mismatch in fused path indexing. Next: minimal C++ repro and audit + CI fuzzing.
